statement: The maximum number of real bitangent lines to a smooth real plane quartic is 28, attained by quartics with four ovals.

answer.qualification: This counts bitangent lines defined over R, including lines whose contact points are conjugate nonreal points.

source.location: Theorem 1.7, PDF p.2; Table 1, PDF p.3

scope: Real projective bitangent lines to smooth real plane quartic curves; the two contact points may be real or a complex-conjugate pair.
notes:
This counts bitangent lines defined over R, including lines whose contact points are conjugate nonreal points.

Originality audit: the real classification is attributed to Zeuthen; Plaumann–Sturmfels–Vinzant is the modern verification source retained in source. Minimum/maximum counts are consequences of that classification. Original Zeuthen text has not been directly checked here.

Related literature. Sur les différentes formes des courbes planes du quatrième ordre (H. G. Zeuthen, 1874). Historical attribution is retained here. The result’s sole article reference identifies the inspected statement or calculation at the recorded locator.

Source discussion. The four-oval case in Theorem 1.7/Table 1 has all 28 bitangents real. The complex count 28 gives the matching upper bound, so the maximum is 28.
